title: A New Approach to Controlling Linear Dynamical Systems
claim: Spectral filter shapes depend strongly on the stability margin: smaller margins give slowly decaying, long-range filters, and larger margins give fast-decaying, localized ones.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared axes, one curve per filter
description: Three side-by-side line plots, one for each value of the stability margin gamma (0.001, 0.01, 0.05). Each plot has the same axes: coordinate index from 0 to 500 on the x-axis and filter value from -0.2 to 0.2 on the y-axis, with a light grid. Each plot shows six colored curves, one for each of the first six eigenvectors of the Hankel matrix, in the default matplotlib palette (blue, orange, green, red, purple, brown). Near the origin the curves oscillate sharply and are clipped by the axis limits. Further out they settle into smooth bumps. At gamma=0.001 the curves decay slowly and stay nonzero out to index 500. At gamma=0.01 they converge to zero near 400. At gamma=0.05 they vanish by about 150. The eye goes first to the tangle of curves at the left of each panel, then to the difference in tail behavior across panels. There is an empty legend box in the top right of each panel.
caption: Entries of the first six eigenvectors of H500, plotted coordinate-wise.
abstract: We propose a new method for controlling linear dynamical systems under adversarial disturbances and cost functions. Our algorithm achieves a running time that scales polylogarithmically with the inverse of the stability margin, improving upon prior methods with polynomial dependence maintaining the same regret guarantees. The technique, which may be of independent interest, is based on a novel convex relaxation that approximates linear control policies using spectral filters constructed from the eigenvectors of a specific Hankel matrix.
